games.title: Plant Part Jobs
games.skillName: Matching plant parts to their jobs
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify and describe the functions of different parts of flowering plants: roots, stem/trunk, leaves and flowers, and investigate the way in which water is transported within plants
games.instruction: Tap the plant part that does each job.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about where that part is on the plant and what it touches, then try again.

questions.ask: Takes in water from the soil
Holds the plant firmly in the ground
Carries water up from the roots to the rest of the plant
Holds the leaves and flowers up towards the light
Uses sunlight to make food for the plant
Wide and flat to catch as much light as possible
Bright and scented to attract insects
The part where seeds are made

games.title: Magnet Match
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to compare and group together a variety of everyday materials on the basis of whether they are attracted to a magnet, and identify some magnetic materials; notice that some forces need contact between two objects, but magnetic forces can act at a distance
games.hint: Not quite. Think about which materials a magnet pulls towards it, then try again.

questions.ask: Which one is NOT attracted to a magnet?
Which one IS attracted to a magnet?
Which of these metals is NOT magnetic?
Which metal object will a magnet NOT pick up?
Which force can act without touching the object?
Which one is NOT true about magnets?
Which surface would a fridge magnet NOT stick to?
Which is the only one a magnet will NOT attract?

games.title: Light and Dark
games.skillName: Knowing we need light to see and how shadows form
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to recognise that they need light in order to see things and that dark is the absence of light; recognise that light from the sun can be dangerous; recognise that shadows are formed when the light from a light source is blocked by an opaque object
games.instruction: Tap True or False for each sentence.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about where light comes from and what happens when it is blocked.

questions.ask: We need light to be able to see things.
Dark is when there is no light.
The Moon is a source of light.
A shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light.
It is safe to look straight at the Sun if you squint.
Light can pass straight through an opaque object.
Your eyes can see things in a room with no light at all.
A mirror reflects light.

games.title: Food and Bones
games.skillName: Nutrition, skeletons and muscles in animals
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to identify that animals, including humans, need the right types and amount of nutrition, and that they cannot make their own food; they get nutrition from what they eat; identify that humans and some other animals have skeletons and muscles for support, protection and movement
games.instruction: Tap the word that fills the gap.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what food gives us and what bones and muscles do, then try again.

questions.ask: Animals cannot make their own ___, so they must eat.
Your skull protects your ___.
Your ribs protect your heart and ___.
Muscles ___ on bones to make them move.
Your skeleton holds your body up and gives it ___.
Meat, fish and beans help our bodies grow and repair because they contain ___.
A worm has no skeleton, so it uses ___ to move.
Eating the right ___ of each type of food helps keep us healthy.

games.title: Seed to Flower
games.skillName: Ordering the life cycle of a flowering plant
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to explore the part that flowers play in the life cycle of flowering plants, including pollination, seed formation and seed dispersal
games.instruction: Tap the step that comes next.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about the life cycle: flowers, pollination, seeds, then spreading the seeds.

questions.ask: Seed → Germination → Seedling → ?
Seedling → Adult plant → Flowers open → ?
Flowers open → Pollination → ?
Bee visits flower → Pollen sticks to bee → Bee flies to another flower → ?
Pollination → Seeds form → Fruit grows → ?
Seeds form → Seed dispersal → Seed lands in soil → ?
Dandelion flower → Fluffy seed head → ?
Bird eats berry → Bird flies far away → ?

games.title: Rock Detective
games.skillName: Identifying rocks and soils from their properties
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to compare and group together different kinds of rocks on the basis of their appearance and simple physical properties; recognise that soils are made from rocks and organic matter
games.instruction: Read the clues and tap what I am.
games.hint: Not quite. Look again at each clue about hardness, grains and what it is used for.

questions.ask: I am made of grains stuck together. I crumble when rubbed. Water soaks into me. What am I?
I am hard with sparkly crystals. Water does not soak in. Kerbs are made of me. What am I?
I am soft and white. You can draw on a pavement with me. What am I?
I split into thin, flat sheets. I am used to make roof tiles. What am I?
I am tiny bits of rock mixed with rotted plants and animals. Plants grow in me. What am I?
I was once a living thing. Over millions of years I turned to rock. What am I?
I am the rotting remains of plants and animals found in soil. What am I?
I am a soil with very tiny bits. I am sticky when wet and hold lots of water. What am I?

games.title: Magnet Moves
games.skillName: Predicting how magnets and surfaces affect movement
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to compare how things move on different surfaces; describe magnets as having two poles; predict whether two magnets will attract or repel each other, depending on which poles are facing
games.instruction: Tap what you think will happen.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about which poles are facing, or how rough the surface is, then try again.

questions.ask: What will happen if you hold the north pole of a magnet near the south pole of another?
What will happen if you push two north poles towards each other?
What happens when you bring a magnet close to, but not touching, a steel paperclip?
What will happen if you hold a magnet next to a plastic cup?
What will happen if you roll a toy car on carpet instead of a smooth floor?
What will happen if you slide a shoe across ice instead of grass?
What will happen if you put a sheet of paper between a magnet and a steel paperclip?
What will happen if you stop pushing a heavy box across a rough floor?

games.title: Fossil Words
games.skillName: Using words about rocks, soils and fossils
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to describe in simple terms how fossils are formed when things that have lived are trapped within rock; recognise that soils are made from rocks and organic matter
games.instruction: Tap the word that matches the meaning.
games.hint: Not quite. Read the meaning again and think about rocks, soil and fossils.

questions.ask: The remains or print of a living thing from long ago, kept in rock
Layers of sand, mud and tiny bits of rock that settle and build up
Describes a rock that lets water soak into it
Describes a rock that does not let water soak into it
Bits of dead plants and animals that rot into the soil
A scientist who studies fossils
The top layer of the ground, made of rock bits and organic matter
A natural solid material made of minerals, such as granite or chalk

games.title: Shiny or Dull
games.skillName: Comparing reflections and the size of shadows
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to notice that light is reflected from surfaces; recognise that light from the sun can be dangerous; find patterns in the way that the size of shadows change
games.instruction: Tap the best answer to each question.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about shiny and dull surfaces, and how close the object is to the light.

questions.ask: Which surface reflects light best?
Which surface reflects the least light?
Which is best for a cyclist to wear so they are easy to see at night?
Which object will make the darkest shadow?
Which material lets the most light through?
A torch shines on a toy. Where should the toy be to make the biggest shadow?
On a sunny day, when is your shadow the longest?
Which is the most dangerous to look straight at?

games.title: Plant Growth Lab
games.skillName: Planning fair tests about plants and surfaces
games.statutoryRequirement: Pupils should be taught to explore the requirements of plants for life and growth (air, light, water, nutrients from soil, and room to grow), setting up simple practical enquiries, comparative and fair tests, and making accurate measurements using standard units
games.instruction: Tap the best choice for each science test.
games.hint: Not quite. Think about what you change, what you keep the same and what you measure.

questions.ask: Which would you use to measure how tall a bean plant grows?
To test if plants need light, what should be different for the two plants?
In a fair test of how water affects plant growth, what must stay the same?
A plant kept in a dark cupboard turns yellow and weak. What can you conclude?
Which is the best way to record a plant's height each week?
How could you see water moving up a celery stalk?
Which would help you see the tiny root hairs on a seedling?
Testing which surface lets a toy car go furthest, what must stay the same?
